subject: Re: Deployment mode and data fencing — keystore & egress checklist
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medsure.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@medsure.com>
Cc: security@medsure.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment mode and data fencing — keystore & egress checklist

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet you and the team. High-level recap from our side and a couple of clarifying asks so we can finalize the internal procurement shortlist:

- Primary requirement: customer-managed key custody for PII processing — we must hold the root keys in our cloud KMS or a dedicated HSM.
- Strong egress restrictions: model outputs and logs need to be allowed to flow only to a small set of approved endpoints (our analytics cluster and S3 bucket in the same VPC).
- Control-plane residency: we'd prefer a deployment where control-plane metadata (audit logs, billing identifiers) does not traverse public Redwood control plane if possible.

Questions:
1) Do you support BYOK with cloud KMS (AWS KMS/CloudHSM) for both Dedicated and Private deployments?
2) Can we enforce egress allow-lists at the host level so no outbound traffic is permitted except to our CIDR ranges?
3) What evidence do you provide for SOC2 and data-residency controls — do you have specific artifacts we can share with our compliance team?

I've attached a one-page summary of our requirements (medsure_requirements.xlsx) for quick reference.

Can you loop in the appropriate technical contact and let me know the earliest slot for a technical deep-dive? We're aiming for a decision by the end of the month.

Best,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Cloud Security, MedSure Health
[Attachment: medsure_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medsure.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode and data fencing — keystore & egress checklist

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the spreadsheet. Looping in Vivek (SE) for the tech specifics and Marissa (AE) for procurement/timing.

Short answers up front so your team can triage:
- BYOK: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS keys (AWS KMS & CloudHSM) and HSM-backed on-prem KMS in air-gapped scenarios. Dedicated has options for customer keys but the control plane is still Redwood-hosted — we can scope the exact custody model.
- Egress controls: Private VPC deployments can be locked down to exact CIDR ranges with egress filtering and private peering. Dedicated environments can also enforce tight egress rules but may require additional network appliances depending on routing.
- SOC2 & evidence: we have SOC2 Type II report, network diagrams, and sample audit logs; I will confirm which artifacts are appropriate to share with your compliance team.

Two quick clarifying questions from our side to make the technical deep-dive efficient:
1) Do you need HSM attestation (e.g., CloudHSM or customer-managed HSM) or is a customer-managed KMS key sufficient?
2) Is the expectation that Redwood instances never have public egress, or that egress is allowed only to our listed endpoints (we'd like the exact CIDRs and FQDNs if possible).

Proposed next steps:
- Vivek: technical deep-dive to map requirements to either Dedicated or Private options.
- Marissa: draft mutual action plan and procurement timeline.
- Elena/Amit: share the compliance window and the list of allowed endpoints.

Available times: Vivek and I can do Wed/Thu in the afternoon PST. Marissa, feel free to update the MAP and send a meeting invite.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medsure.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 13:45:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode and data fencing — keystore & egress checklist

Elena, Lauren — quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive so we can prepare materials. Below is an operational comparison and the gating items we'll need from MedSure to validate each path.

Option A — Redwood Private (VPC-hosted control plane or fully customer-controlled):
- BYOK: Full support. We can integrate with AWS KMS keys owned by MedSure; keys can be configured such that key material never leaves your KMS. For HSM-grade requirements we support CloudHSM and partner HSMs — customers can bring their own HSM (BYOHSM) and we can integrate via a private connection.
- Control-plane residency: Optional — we offer a private control-plane deployment where metadata and billing telemetry can be routed through your VPC.
- Egress & networking: We deploy inference pods in your VPC/subnet. Egress is controllable via security groups + subnet NACLs. For strict blocking we recommend a combination of (1) forced NAT through your managed NAT gateway with strict egress rules and (2) host-level iptables rules applied by our operators where required.
- Audit evidence: we can provide deployment diagrams, audit log samples filtered for your tenant, and a runbook for key rotation and HSM attestations.

Option B — Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, Redwood-managed control plane):
- BYOK: Supported to an extent — we can accept wrapped keys and integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest. However the control plane remains Redwood-hosted, which means some telemetry will be visible to Redwood. If your policy forbids ANY control-plane telemetry leaving MedSure, Dedicated may not meet your constraints.
- Egress & networking: We support VPC peering and private connectivity for data ingress/egress; however, some operational management paths (agent telemetry, autoscaling signals) use our control plane. We can pin and scope what flows to the control plane during design.
- Audit evidence: SOC2 report + tenancy diagrams. For customers requiring HSM attestation or complete control plane residency, Private is typically the path.

Gating items / what we need from MedSure to finalize a recommended path:
1) Confirmation: Is control-plane residency a hard MUST? (i.e., no telemetry/billing metadata may leave MedSure)
2) List of required endpoint CIDRs/FQDNs for allowed egress (we'll validate how many rules it equates to).
3) KMS/HSM preference: AWS KMS, CloudHSM, or on-prem HSM. If on-prem HSM, we need network reachability details.
4) Compliance artifacts requested: specific SOC2 sections or logs that your auditors will require.

Attachments I'm dropping into the thread: redwood_private_byo_kms_notes.pdf (technical notes), example_egress_patterns.png (diagram). I'll prepare a short demo of the VPC deployment topology for the deep-dive.

— Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_private_byo_kms_notes.pdf (pdf)]

Elena — thanks, all. Capturing the agreed next steps so we have a single action list: 
1) MedSure to confirm control-plane residency requirement (is "no telemetry leaves MedSure" a blocker?). Owner: Elena. Due: 2026-12-04.
2) MedSure to share allowed CIDRs/FQDNs and the compliance window / SOC2 audit scope. Owner: Amit. Due: 2026-12-06.
3) Redwood to deliver a 45-minute technical deep-dive (Vivek) + VPC topology diagram and key custody runbook. Proposed slots: Thu 12/3 11:00-12:00 PST or Fri 12/4 14:00-14:45 PST.
4) Redwood to provide initial MAP and preliminary SOW draft for procurement review. Owner: Marissa. Due: 2026-12-07.

I'll attach the MAP and SOW stub. If the control-plane residency is a firm requirement, our recommendation will be to pursue Redwood Private with BYOK/HSM integration. If not, Dedicated with strict egress rules could be a faster path to production.

I'll send a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive once Elena confirms the preferred slot.

Best — Marissa
